cases.title: Aggression against Ukraine — March 2022
cases.proposal_summary: The draft condemns the aggression against Ukraine and demands that Russia end its use of force and withdraw its forces.
cases.statement_summary: China said the resolution lacked sufficient consultation and attention to security concerns and diplomatic settlement; it abstained. It also affirmed respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity.
cases.setting: The General Assembly's eleventh emergency special session considered a draft on Russia's use of force against Ukraine after the Security Council referred the issue to the Assembly under the Uniting for Peace procedure.
cases.decision_rule: Recorded General Assembly vote on the draft; the resolution is a collective Assembly decision, not a treaty or a negotiated bilateral agreement.

clauses.text: Reaffirms Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders.
Deplores Russia's aggression and demands an immediate end to force and a complete, unconditional withdrawal.
Rejects Russia's recognition of separatist areas in Donetsk and Luhansk and demands reversal.
Calls for civilian protection, safe passage, humanitarian access and observance of humanitarian law.
Urges political dialogue, negotiation and mediation to resolve the conflict peacefully.

national_position.speaker: Zhang Jun, China
positions: Affirmed respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity.
Said the draft had not received full membership consultation and did not sufficiently address the crisis's history and complexity.
Argued that indivisible security and diplomatic settlement deserved more emphasis; explicitly linked these concerns to China's abstention.
national_position.synthesis: China affirmed the sovereignty principle in OP1 and supported diplomatic settlement in OP14–15, but its post-vote explanation objected to consultation and to the draft's treatment of security concerns. It explicitly connected those stated objections to abstaining; it did not reject every provision.
national_position.evidence_limit: This is a post-vote explanation of China's stated reasons. It cannot be placed in a pre-vote prediction prompt. It does not establish a private bargaining threshold.

cases.title: Territorial integrity of Ukraine — October 2022
cases.proposal_summary: The draft rejects the referendums and attempted annexation, calls for non-recognition, demands reversal and withdrawal, and supports peaceful resolution.
cases.statement_summary: Before the vote, China argued that the draft would not advance de-escalation, resumed dialogue or a political settlement, and explicitly said it would abstain. It also called for humanitarian relief and attention to spillover harms, especially for developing countries.
cases.setting: The resumed emergency special session considered a draft after Russia's September 2022 referendums and attempted annexation of four Ukrainian regions.
cases.decision_rule: The Assembly applied a two-thirds majority of members present and voting to this recorded vote.

clauses.text: Reaffirms Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity within internationally recognized borders.
Condemns the referendums and attempted annexation, declaring the acts invalid as a basis for changing regional status.
Calls on states and organizations not to recognize any altered status of Donetsk, Kherson, Luhansk or Zaporizhzhia.
Demands reversal of the status decisions and complete, unconditional withdrawal of Russian forces.
Supports humanitarian response and de-escalation through dialogue, negotiation and other peaceful means.

national_position.speaker: Geng Shuang, China
positions: Called for resumed talks, humanitarian protection and relief, and limits on food, energy and economic spillovers affecting developing countries.
Said Assembly action should help de-escalation and political settlement; explicitly said this draft would not do so and China would abstain.
Reaffirmed respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity while raising procedural fairness and security concerns.
national_position.synthesis: China's representative affirmed sovereignty but said the October draft would not advance de-escalation and resumed talks, then announced an intended abstention. OP6–7 do include humanitarian and diplomatic language; the public objection therefore concerns the draft's overall effect as China stated it, not the total absence of those topics.
national_position.evidence_limit: This pre-vote statement explicitly announces and explains the intended abstention. It is therefore outcome-leaking evidence for a vote-prediction task, though valid context for a retrospective report.

prompt.content: Report only what the supplied historical evidence establishes. Do not infer private motives or bargaining conditions.
